A language is a lexicon of words that various characters use to speak to each other and communicate. In World of Warcraft, most races have a unique language they speak that only they can understand. Each faction shares a common language of the dominant race (Orcish for Horde and Common for Alliance). A language may or may not have an associated alphabet for writing. Several languages may share the same alphabet, or may have a specific alphabet used only for that language. Lorewise, there are at least 39 languages on Azeroth and hundreds more throughout the cosmos. Lands of Conflict is a sourcebook for the Warcraft RPG. It was published in 2004. It is one of five known volumes (the others being Lands of Mystery and portions of Alliance Player's Guide, Horde Player's Guide, and Dark Factions) written by Brann Bronzebeard during his journeys around the world. Lands of Conflict covers his journeys in the Eastern Kingdoms. The events in Lands of Conflict take place before the source book World of Warcraft The Roleplaying Game, and just after the events of the Frozen Throne and Daelin Proudmoore's attack on Durotar.

Lake Al'Ameth is one of the largest bodies of water existing on Teldrassil. It is located just south of Dolanaar, though contains few fixtures apart from a small jetty. Lately, many enraged timberlings have been sighted on the shores of the lake, and it is no longer safe.

Lands of Mystery is a sourcebook for the World of Warcraft RPG. It was published in 2006. It is one of five known volumes (the others being Lands of Conflict, portions of the Alliance Player's Guide, Horde Player's Guide, and Dark Factions) written by Brann Bronzebeard during his journeys around the world after the events of Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne. It covers his journeys in Kalimdor, the Southern Seas, and Northrend.

Lake Kel'Theril is a small frozen lake in central Winterspring. The shores of the lake are home to the Ruins of Kel'Theril, which along with the lake itself is populated by many tormented spirits of the Highborne. Adventurers came here to hunt ectoplasm for their tier 0.5 armor quests. During the periodic Elemental Invasions Princess Tempestria spawned here.

.]] The Lakkari Tar Pits are lakes of thick, foul-smelling black tar pits found in northern Un'Goro Crater, just below Marshal's Refuge. Flowers, Tarblossoms grow at the bottom of these pits, which have gone unnoticed for a long time. Tar beasts live in the area among several giant bones of creatures that got stuck here. The only creatures that remain around the Lakkari Tar Pits are those that get stuck in its grip and scavengers looking for easy prey. The bones of hundreds of beasts jut out from the surface of the tar strewn across the shore.

and her banshee choir performing the lament.]] The Lament of the Highborne (item) is a small book that contains the Thalassian song of the same name. The Lament of Captain Placeholder was a song created for the beta NPC Captain Placeholder after Blizzard had removed him from the game. The song was written and recorded in 2005 by a dedicated player going by the alias Eledainn, and was later covered by Cranius. Lantresor of the Blade is a half-orc quest giver located at the Burning Blade Ruins in Nagrand. He is a half-draenei, half-orc blademaster and leader of the ogre Boulderfist clan of Outland, and of the orcish Burning Blade clan. He is said to have crossed the Dark Portal, serving under two Warchiefs of the Horde and later returning home. By the time he arrives at the first Azerothian Kosh'harg festival, he has assumed leadership of the Burning Blade by virtue of being the eldest surviving blademaster. Laos Flipor was a jester in the Court of Lordaeron under of the kingdom of Stormwind. She had a reputation in the Court, it was said, for bad jokes and poor taste. When orcs invaded Azeroth, and the Second War began, she was fond of telling the following joke: Orc walks into a bar, leaves his axe at the door. Barman: Hey! You can't leave that lyin' there! Orc: That no lion, that's an axe! Unfortunately, Flipor was later murdered by Arthas Menethil when he murdered his father, apparently because after being corrupted by Frostmourne, he lost his sense of humor. .]] Lake Wintergrasp is a vast frozen lake and the largest body of water in all Northrend. This lake sits midway up and just west of the Dragonblight proper, and the ground there is low and even, and frozen solid. Although there is no knowledge whether the lake has always been frozen, it probably has, since Icecrown Glacier is right above it. Lake Wintergrasp effectively shields the Borean Tundra, which runs into the lake on the tundra's northern border, from the Dragonblight and Icecrown Glacier. A pack of Icemist tauren settled on the western edge of the Dragonblight, on the lake's shore, in a settlement called Icemist Village. Murlocs have settled the lake too. The surface is frozen solid

The Lair of the Jade Witch is the home to Widow Greenpaw, known as the "Jade Witch" by the locals due to all the jade statues around the house. This area within the Forest Heart of the Jade Forest is a shrine to Master Greenpaw, the first Jade Fist Monk, whose fighting style was legendary.

Lake Kittitata is a large lake in northwest Jade Forest, and one of the sources that create the Serenity Falls and the Slicky Stream. The hozen often used this lake to fish in to feed their people, however, during certain seasons of the year crocolisks claim the lake as home and feed upon the hozen that get too close. Camp Nooka Nooka is on the lake's southeastern border. The Circle of Scale lies at the center of the lake.

The Lair of Gonk is the shrine in the Garden of the Loa in Zuldazar dedicated to the loa, Gonk. The entrance is a devilsaur skull and is guarded by Gonk's children.
The Lair of Rezan is a cave at the top of the Temple of Rezan, near the throne. Atal'zul cultists corrupt one of the children of Rezan.
Lancet of the Deft Hand drops from G'huun and the following trash mobs in Uldir: *Blightspreader Tendril *Cyclopean Terror *Dark Young

Lady Warcrest's Music Box drops from Lord and Lady Waycrest in Waycrest Manor.

The Lamp is located on a shelf at Thalassian Pass of Ghostlands during the Writing on the Wall. A plaque can be found above it.
Lake Crocolisks are crocolisks located in Elwynn Forest during On Track.

The language of death is a secret language known to all Scourge and Cult of the Damned members. To outsiders, its existence was never proven until the war against the Lich King, where forces of the Alliance and Horde found Flesh-bound Tomes written in blood and using the language. They were translated in order to decypher the Scourge plans in the Dragonblight.
Lancer-Captain Blaer is a Forsaken located in Lor'danel Landing in Darkshore. She also participates in the Battle for Darkshore.
Lakeshire Handwraps are rewarded from Surveying Equipment (quest).
Lady Zharessa is a naga centaur located at the Tidal Conflux in Nazjatar where she guards the :Tidestone of Golganneth.
Lang's Hand Grenades are provided as an objective for the following quests: *Araj the Summoner (Alliance) *The Endless Flow (Alliance)

The Landward Cannon is a cannon located aboard Fortune's Fist of the coast of the Swamp of Sorrows. Using it will send you back to land, right by Lil' Crazy Jerry and The Baron's Cannon... most of the time.
Lake Snappers are turtles located in and around Lake Elrendar in Eversong Woods.
Laestrite Ore is mined from Laestrite Deposits in the Shadowlands.
Laestrite Deposits can be found in the Shadowlands. These veins can be mined for Laestrite Ore.

The Lady of the Falls is a faerie located at Glitterfall Basin in Ardenweald. As the droman of the basin, she puts the safety of the people under her care above all else. To those who threaten her people or assault her lands, she responds with swift retribution. She was present during The Battle of Ardenweald.
Landing Boats are boats located in Tiragarde Sound. Some are carrying Burnsy the Blade, Wiley Jaki, and Skullcrusher Cotner. The boats are sailed by Irontide Pillagers.

Lando'sal is a jungle troll located on the second floor of the Wyvern's Tail in Orgrimmar. He is sharing a table with Barra the Quick.

Larati is a tuskarr butcher from Taruka's clan. She is a friend of Taruka and regularly exchanges insults with the catch master Kattik. After only receiving one knot from Kattik as reward for her catch of seven yellowtail, Taruka headed over to Larati, who insulted Kattik as usual but admitted that no other catch master would've given Taruka more knots. The butcher did not believe Taruka's claim that she would catch more and bigger fish.
